max_tire.note: It leaves the factory on 37s with 420 mm of clearance. We found no owner reports of fitting bigger tires.

timeline.change: JGSDF begins trials of the High Mobility Vehicle. A civilian prototype is shown at the 30th Tokyo Motor Show in October
Regular HMV deliveries begin with the 1st Infantry Regiment in spring. Civilian production starts late in the year
9 January: civilian Mega Cruiser (BXD20V) goes on sale at Toyota Store dealers. 15B-FT, 155 PS, ¥9.62 million
May: civilian truck switches to the electronically injected 15B-FTE (170 PS, 43.0 kgm); price ¥9.8 million. The HMV gets the same engine from FY1999
Civilian production ends in August and sales in December, after 133 registrations
HMV moves to Hino's N04C engine as the XCD10. Later military trucks are not BXD10s
The earliest trucks pass 25 years old and become legal to import into the US
Japan delivers 30 HMVs to Ukraine as part of a vehicle donation

identify.intro: With 133 civilian trucks and thousands of military ones, knowing exactly which Mega Cruiser you're looking at decides what it's worth.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: BXD20V (full type KC-BXD20V-RRPEW) is the civilian five-door wagon. BXD10 is the 15B-engined JGSDF High Mobility Vehicle. XCD10 is the later HMV with a Hino N04C engine, built from FY2004.

items.head: Civilian vs military
items.body: Civilian trucks have a hard roof, six seats, air conditioning, a right-hinged side-opening tailgate with a retractable step, and a chain hoist for the high-mounted spare. Military BXD10s typically have canvas tops, inward-facing rear benches, a folding windscreen and run-flat inserts in the tires.

items.head: High roof
items.body: Some civilian trucks had a high roof that wasn't in the catalogue. BaT's 2025 high-roof truck had a fiberglass roof with hatches and safari windows.

items.head: Engine
items.body: 15B-FT (mechanical injection) on 1996 to April 1999 civilian trucks, and 15B-FTE (electronic injection) from May 1999.

items.head: Drive side
items.body: Toyota built the Mega Cruiser in right-hand drive. Carscoops put the left-hand-drive count at around twelve in 2020, and one BaT seller claimed seven.

values.intro: Very thin market. Civilian wagons fetch six figures, while ex-military soft-tops have struggled to meet their reserves.
values.note: Based on seven Bring a Trailer listings, January 2024 – June 2025: sold for $167,500 (Jan 2024) and $84,000 (high roof, June 2025). Bid without selling: $144,000 (LHD), $85,300, $82,000, $43,999 and $32,025.

paragraphs: Toyota sold the Mega Cruiser new only in Japan. Some reached Australia, Russia, Kenya and the Philippines as gray imports. NHTSA's 25-year exemption made the first trucks legal to import into the US from 2020–21, and BaT trucks have carried Florida, New Hampshire, Georgia and Maryland titles.

Ex-military BXD10s come out through third countries, so check the paperwork carefully: one BaT truck was repainted in Dubai and titled in Maryland as a 1990 model. Check your state's emissions and titling rules before you buy. In Japan, the truck's 3,780 kg gross weight puts it beyond the standard car licence for drivers licensed after March 2017.

production.intro: Civilian production was tiny. The military HMV, in later forms, is still being built.

items.v: More than 3,000 including derivatives (BXD10 and later XCD10), still in procurement
